review_candidates.description: Philanthropy Gift Officer (PGO) Global Giving | Philanthropy Team | Remote -45% Travel POSITION SUMMARY The Philanthropy Gift Officer (PGO) position is responsible for strategically stewarding, cultivating, retaining, and growing a portfolio of rising, major, and signature donor relationships. This role connects donor passions and philanthropic goals with MAP’s mission, delivering meaningful engagement opportunities that inspire generosity and deepen commitment. With a focus on individual revenue and expense goals tied to the assigned portfolio, the PGO will manage a portfolio of rising to signature donors (cumulative gifts of $5,000+), ensuring high retention, increased giving, and enhanced donor involvement. By providing personalized engagement, thoughtful stewardship, and compelling investment opportunities for impact, the PGO plays a vital role in advancing MAP’s mission and enabling donors to fulfill their vision for global health. ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES •    Manage a portfolio of assigned donors ($5,000+ cumulative gifts annually), ensuring high retention, increased giving, and deeper engagement. •    Cultivate, steward, and grow relationships with a portfolio of approximately 90–150 rising, major, and signature donors, including individuals, family foundations, and organizations. •    Develop and implement personalized engagement strategies that align donor passions with MAP International’s mission and priorities. •    Gather and share accurate, compelling proposals, followed by impact stories and data that demonstrate how contributions are used and the difference they make locally and globally. •    Represent MAP at select high-level donor engagements, events, and gatherings to deepen relationships with rising, major, and signature donors. •    Advance prospecting efforts to identify and research new high-capacity individuals, family foundations, and organizations, building a robust pipeline through strategic outreach and early cultivation activities. •    Pursue daily communication with portfolio donors through phone calls, emails, and mail to steward them for gifts, share the impact of their giving, invite them to special events, and communicate urgent needs. Develop relationships with donors to understand their passions and communicate MAP’s mission and continuing efforts. •    Conduct regular in-person visits and virtual meetings with donors and partners, ensuring timely follow-up and meaningful connection. •    Partner with internal teams to coordinate messaging, donor materials, and stewardship efforts for consistency and excellence. •    Maintain MAP’s CRM system, currently Agilon ONE, daily to capture donor interactions and communications and allow for effective reporting. •    Follow the moves management plan for each donor, which serves as a foundational communication and marketing plan, faithfully and on a timely basis so that individuals in the portfolio are retained and upgraded. •    Be an active member of the Philanthropy team within Global Giving, which consists of Philanthropy, Direct Response, and Marketing. ORGANIZATIONAL RELATIONSHIPS Reports to the Vice President of Development and is a member of the Philanthropy team within Global Giving. The position interfaces with the following internal teams: Office of the President, Finance, Operations, IT, Human Resources, Foundations Gift Officer, Marketing, Direct Response Officer, and Corporate Relations. The Philanthropy Gift Officer does not have any supervisory responsibilities. QUALIFICATIONS To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. This is a remote position, so access to an appropriate home-based workspace is required. •    Ability to qualify donors from the larger pool of organizational donors that meet the rising, major, and signature gift criteria. •    Ability to create reasonable financial goals for each donor based on their giving and potential. •    Ability to create a personal contact and ask plan for each donor in the portfolio, considering the individual donor’s interests, motivations, giving patterns, and ask preferences, in a timely and cost-effective manner. •    Ability to retain and upgrade donors. •    Ability to ask for gifts from qualified donors (rising $5,000–$9,999; major $10,000–$99,999; signature $100,000+). •    Ability to secure project and organization information and create and write effective investment opportunity proposals. •    Ability to gather and provide accurate, compelling information to report back to donors on the impact of their contributions. •    Ability to manage processes, deadlines, and budget while adhering to the policies and procedures of the organization. •    Ability to maintain a positive and constructive attitude while solving problems. •    Ability to be a team player and protect the mission, goals, and values of the organization. •    Excellent written and verbal communication skills. •    An excellent relationship builder and sustainer, able to thrive in MAP’s “relationship model” of development. •    An independent worker able to multitask and handle work-related stress. •    Ability to accurately enter, update, and maintain donor information in the CRM, ensuring data integrity, consistency, and timely processing to support effective fundraising and relationship management. EDUCATION AND/OR EXPERIENCE •    Bachelor’s degree required, or equivalent work experience. •    Experience in a field conducive to strong written and verbal communication skills required. •    A basic knowledge of international relief and development work, health conditions overseas, and/or nonprofit business skills. •    Moderate to advanced computer skills required, with proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Outlook, Word, PowerPoint). •    Experience with donor databases (e.g., Agilon, Salesforce, Raiser’s Edge, or similar) required. •    A minimum of 3 years of successful rising, major, and signature gift fundraising experience from individuals, foundations, churches, and organizations, preferably in the international NGO and relief sector. •    Fundraising experience that has shown results, with a proven track record of achieving and surpassing targets. OTHER SKILLS AND ABILITIES •    Strong interpersonal communication skills, especially strong listening skills. •    Self-motivated, with a positive attitude and demonstrated self-accountability. •    Experience that exemplifies being a team player with a service-oriented mindset and a proactive approach to problem solving and critical thinking. •    Ability to work independently and remotely. •    Demonstrated ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment. •    Excellent organizational skills, with the ability to successfully manage multiple tasks. •    Confident, innovative self-starter, able to work independently with high energy and excitement. •    Ability to work well in a team environment. •    Excellent administrative and organizational skills. •    Moderate to advanced knowledge of CRM systems and Microsoft Office Suite. •     Ability to travel up to 45% of the time. •    Ability to excite, inspire, and motivate colleagues, donors, and volunteers. •    Proactive and flexible approach with a positive, professional attitude. •    Passion for philanthropy and the mission of MAP. PHYSICAL DEMANDS The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand; walk; sit; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms; and talk or hear. The employee must be able to travel. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, color vision, and the ability to adjust focus during significant computer-related work. The employee must be able to read, write, and speak English fluently.
